nodes.name: Hollow core-shell PBA synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, 0.746 g Ni(CH₃CO₂)₂·4H₂O, 0.980 g Mn(CH₃CO₂)₂·4H₂O, and 3.087 g sodium citrate dihydrate were added in 100 mL of deionized water with stirring for 30 minutes to obtain solution A. 0.066 g K₃[Fe(CN)₆] and 0.066 g K₃[Co(CN)₆] were added in another 40 mL of deionized water with stirring for 5 min to obtain solution B. Solution B was added dropwise into solution A under stirring for 5 min. Subsequently, the mixture was aged for 24 h to get precipitate. After centrifuging and washing twice with deionized water, the product was dried overnight in vacuum at 70°C.

nodes.description: OER chronopotentiometry stability on Ni foam
nodes.source_text: The chronopotentiometric measurement for OER with FeMn@CoNi-H/NF electrode (FeMn@CoNi-H coated on Ni foam, 1×1cm²) was performed at 300mA cm^{-2} for 40h. As shown in Figure 6f, the FeMn@CoNi-H/NF provided excellent stability with small voltage amplification (≈18mV) after 40h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hollow FeMn@CoNi-H nanoparticles assume a cubic shape with average particle size of 73.1 nm; their hollow nature exposed by broken nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1a,b, and S1, Supporting Information, hollow FeMn@CoNi-H nanoparticles (NPs) assumed a cubic shape with an average particle size of 73.1 nm and their hollow nature was exposed by some of the broken nanocages in the SEM and TEM images.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals hollow nature of FeMn@CoNi-H with cubic shape; solid FeMn@CoNi-S shows uniform cubic shape with larger size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: hollow FeMn@CoNi-H nanoparticles (NPs) assumed a cubic shape with an average particle size of 73.1 nm and their hollow nature was exposed by some of the broken nanocages in the SEM and TEM images.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF and EDS mapping confirm cavity and heterogeneous chemical distributions in FeMn@CoNi-H with Fe/Mn in core and Co/Ni in shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) and EDS mapping (Figure 1c) confirmed the cavity and heterogeneous chemical distributions.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows crystal lattice spacing of (200) facets: FeMn-rich core at 0.523 nm and outer shell at 0.514 nm for FeMn@CoNi-H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a closer inspection of the FeMn@CoNi-H (Inverse IFFT image) revealed that the crystal lattice spacing, corresponding to (200) facets, of the FeMn-rich core was slightly greater at 0.523 nm than that of the outer shell at 0.514 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern displays typical face-centered cubic (FCC) diffraction spots of (002), (004), and (022) with identically oriented lattices.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern collected from a single particle displayed typical face-centered cubic (FCC) diffraction spots of (002), (004), and (022) (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples display FCC structure (Fm3m) with main peaks at 17.2°, 24.4°, 34.8°, 39.0° assigned to (200), (220), (400), (420) planes; core-shell samples show intermediate peak positions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the samples displayed FCC structure (space group Fm3m), consistent with the characteristics of classic PBAs. Four main peaks located around the 17.2°, 24.4°, 34.8°, and 39.0° could be assigned to the (200), (220), (400), and (420) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeMn PBA shows ν(CN) bands at 2080 and 2122 cm⁻¹ (Fe-CN-Mn); CoNi shows 2193 and 2210 cm⁻¹ (Co-CN-Ni); core-shell samples exhibit both with blueshift/redshift due to strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For FeMn PBA, there were two obvious ν(CN) bands at 2080 and 2122 cm⁻¹, which are assigned to the respective Fe-CN-Mn species. In addition, two peaks were observed at 2193 and 2210 cm⁻¹; they were merged and became pronounced on the broad peak, indicating the Co-CN-Ni species of cyanide complexes.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS measurements reveal surface chemical bonding states: Fe mainly as Fe²⁺ in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ (Fe 2p₃/₂ 708.2 eV, 2p₁/₂ 721.0 eV); Co in bivalent states; Ni mainly Ni²⁺ with minor Ni³⁺; Mn in +2/+3 states for both FeMn@CoNi-H and FeMn@CoNi-S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, for the Fe 2p spectrum, the main peaks were assigned to Fe²⁺ 2p₃/₂(708.2 eV) and 2p₁/₂(721.0 eV), indicating that the Fe was mainly present in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻. ... the obtained high-resolution XPS spectra of Fe 2p, Co 2p, Ni 2p, and Mn 2p over FeMn@CoNi-H and FeMn@CoNi-S are similar with the fitting of various metal peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: Specific surface area calculated from nitrogen adsorption isotherms using BET model (data in Figures S22 and S23).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area of the samples was calculated from the nitrogen adsorption isotherms measured with Quantachrome Autosorb IQ3 based on the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) model.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis absorption spectrum of FeMn@CoNi-H lies between those of FeMn PBA and CoNi PBA, indicating heterogeneous chemical composition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their UV-vis absorption spectrum lied between those of FeMn PBA, and CoNi PBA (Figure S2, Supporting Information), indicating the heterogeneity of the chemical composition.
